message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the major long‑weekend holidays that Canadians typically enjoy in 2023. (Note that some holidays are provincial, so the exact dates may differ slightly depending on where you live.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Typical Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|---------------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Sunday, Jan 1 | **Jan 1–3** (Fri–Sun) |
| **Family Day** (Alberta, BC, NB, ON, SK) | Monday, Feb 20 | **Feb 18–20** (Wed–Mon) |
| **Good Friday** (most provinces) | Friday, Apr 7 | **Apr 7–9** (Fri–Sun) |
| **Victoria Day** (all provinces) | Monday, May 22 | **May 20–22** (Wed–Mon) |
| **Canada Day** (all provinces) | Saturday, Jul 1 | **Jul 1–3** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Labour Day** (all provinces) | Monday, Sep 4 | **Sep 2–4** (Wed–Mon) |
| **Thanksgiving** (all provinces) | Monday, Oct 9 | **Oct 7–9** (Wed–Mon) |
| **Remembrance Day** (all provinces) | Monday, Nov 11 | **Nov 9–11** (Wed–Mon) |
| **Christmas Day** (all provinces) | Monday, Dec 25 | **Dec 23–25** (Wed–Mon) |
| **Boxing Day** (all provinces) | Tuesday, Dec 26 | **Dec 26–28** (Tue–Thu) |

These are the federal holidays that usually give Canadians a three‑day break. If you’re looking at a specific province, you might also want to add provincial holidays such as St. Patrick’s Day (Ontario, Feb 17) or St. John’s Day (Manitoba, Mar 17) – they can sometimes create additional short long weekends depending on the weekday they fall on.
